text:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to decide the preemption window behavior for APAC reserved pools pilot. How aggressive do we want preemption vs. honoring burst credits?
Sam: My read: APAC latency is spiky for a few pilot customers. If we preempt too fast they blow past their SLOs. Maybe longer soft-window? :thinking_face:
Leo: Agree. Proposal: 5m soft preempt (notifications + graceful drain), 30m hard reclaim. Soft allows app-level fallback.
Irene: 5m soft feels long when capacity is tight. Ops said last Friday a 2m soft would've freed GPUs for a big job.
Anika: Customer ask (Lighthouse APAC) was explicit: no sudden throttles during business hours. They prefer graceful degradation, even if slightly higher cost.
Sam: Can we gate behavior by customer tier + time-of-day? e.g., during 9–6 local, apply 5m soft + best-effort spillover; off hours 2m.
Maya: That sounds like policy complexity. What's the incremental engineering work? Rough estimate?
Leo: ~2 wks infra + 1 wk product to expose toggles and a rollout plan. Need autoscale hooks to avoid oscillation.
Irene: Also need observability: per-tenant preempt events, time-to-reclaim histogram, and a quick dashboard for oncall.
Anika: For contract/legal: if we promise burst guarantees in pilot, we mustn't preempt without notice. Need a canary policy for contracted tenants.
Sam: Proposed launch criteria for pilot: (1) toggleable preempt window per pool, (2) dashboard with event feed, (3) customer-facing doc + opt-in toggle, (4) alerting on >3 preempts/hour for a tenant.
Maya: Sounds reasonable. Can we add an automated fallback: if a tenant experiences >X preempts in Y minutes, temporarily escalate them to a higher burst tier while we triage?
Leo: Technically doable: temporary credit bump + cooldown. Complexity + billing implications though.
Irene: Billing team will want a clear rule for temporary credit grants and how they affect invoicing. Ops-bot should log these as audit events.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout queued for staging at 2026-04-02T02:00Z — will include preempt-toggle flag.
Anika: Risk notes: (a) Too many policy knobs -> confusion; (b) cross-region spillover may create hard network latency issues; (c) billing edge cases.
Maya: Decision time: Do we accept the gated-time-of-day + tier policy for pilot and scope the temp-credit bump as a post-launch experiment? Vote: +1 accept pilot scope, -1 push more product work first.
Sam: +1
Leo: +1
Irene: -1 (want shorter soft window by default)
Anika: +1
Maya: +1 (but add a follow-up ticket to define billing rules)
Maya: Outcome: proceed with pilot: implement per-pool preempt window toggle, time-of-day gating, dashboards, canary rollout. Temp-credit bump is deferred to a follow-up experiment and billing spec.
Maya: Action items: (1) Leo to create infra PR + estimate (due EOD Thursday); (2) Irene to draft dashboard spec and alert thresholds; (3) Anika to coordinate pilot opt-in doc + customer comms; (4) Sam to draft launch criteria and canary plan.
Leo: Will post PR link and rough changelog by EOD.
Irene: Adding dashboard stub to our internal Confluence page.
Anika: I'll reach out to Lighthouse APAC and confirm they can opt into canary.
Sam: I'll draft the launch checklist in the product repo — will ping for review.
Maya: Thanks team. We'll reconvene on Friday 11am PT for a pre-canary readout.
